subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should native backup excludes be an explicit per-run feature only, or may PR #44288 change default backup scope by auto-loading `stateDir/.backupignore` and warning when external assets bypass excludes?
rationale: This changes backup data selection and recovery/security semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent core policy or accept warning-only gaps on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Require explicit and complete excludes
options.body: Make `.backupignore` loading opt-in or separately approved, apply filters per asset root, and preserve gitignore semantics before merge.

options.title: Accept the broader PR contract
options.body: Maintain the implicit `.backupignore` behavior and warning-only external-asset limitation as a deliberate core policy with documented upgrade impact.

options.title: Pause or replace the PR
options.body: Keep #40786 open and ask for a narrower implementation that only adds explicit `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` first.

recommendation.title: Require explicit and complete excludes
recommendation.body: Make `.backupignore` loading opt-in or separately approved, apply filters per asset root, and preserve gitignore semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original backup CLI and authored the infra extraction, so they are the best history-backed owner for the backup contract decision.
